```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  echo = FALSE,
  fig.width = 7,

  dpi = 150,
  message = FALSE,

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
# the figures' palette: the mark's black and greys with one steel-blue accent (Al, 2026-11-05); it moves to gq's palette
# registry when that exists
pal <- c(ink = "#1a1a1a", mid = "#8c8c8c", light = "#d9d9d9", soft = "#bdbdbd", accent = "#3a6b8c", grey = "#9a9a9a")
```

```{r load}
# data from data-raw/vignette_cut_points.R and data-raw/vignette_cut_points_places.R
vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "knowledge", mustWork = TRUE)
x <- readRDS(vd("cut_points.rds"))
pl <- readRDS(vd("cut_points_places.rds"))
# the places were measured on this bundle
stopifnot(identical(pl$meta$bundle_md5, unname(tools::md5sum(vd("cut_points.rds")))))
places <- pl$places

# formatting
n0 <- function(v) format(round(v), big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
pc <- function(v, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * v, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
grad <- function(g, d = 1) paste0(formatC(100 * g, format = "f", digits = d), " %")
lim <- function(g) paste0(signif(100 * g, 3), " %")
link_site <- "https://www.newgraphenvironment.com/link/"
research <- "https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/knowledge/blob/main/research/minimal_network_tuning.md"
where <- function(p) {
  r <- places[places$place == p$place & places$site_visit %in% p$site_visit, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  nm <- if (is.na(r$gnis_name)) "an unnamed stream" else r$gnis_name
  via <- if (r$joins_direct) "flowing into" else "draining to"
  sprintf("%s %s the %s, %s km %s of %s", nm, via, r$joins, n0(r$town_km), r$compass, r$town)
}

# ---- the premise: sites that start a segment of their own ----------------------------------------------------------
pm <- x$premise
pm_at <- function(n, cs) pm$at_site_pct[pm$network == n & pm$catch_status == cs] / 100
stopifnot(nrow(pm) == 6, all(c("published_92", "published_145", "minimal") %in% pm$network))
# the same visits on each network, so the footnote's counts hold for every row
stopifnot(all(tapply(pm$visits, pm$catch_status, function(v) length(unique(v)) == 1)))
# the sentences: on both full networks a site with fish starts its own segment far more often than one without; on
# the minimal network the two are close
stopifnot(pm_at("published_145", "fish") > 5 * pm_at("published_145", "zero"),
          pm_at("published_92", "fish") > 5 * pm_at("published_92", "zero"),
          abs(pm_at("minimal", "fish") - pm_at("minimal", "zero")) < 0.01,
          pm_at("published_145", "fish") / pm_at("published_92", "fish") > 0.4,
          pm_at("published_145", "fish") / pm_at("published_92", "fish") < 0.6)

# ---- the setups --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
su <- x$setups
s_of <- function(s) su[su$setup == s, ]
stopifnot(identical(su$setup, c("published", "minimal", "parent", "atlas")), length(unique(su$n_visits)) == 1)
in_reg <- function(pick_of, region_of) {
  t <- x$tune[[region_of]]
  v <- t$in_region[t$rule == s_of(pick_of)$pick]
  stopifnot(length(v) == 1)
  v == "TRUE"
}
# the opening's words: 13 % on the full network, 9 % on the minimal, the 13 % no close call on the minimal network's
# records and the 9 % a close call on the full network's; the parent setup picks the minimal network's rule exactly,
# the Atlas line a steeper limit; every pick keeps the flow floor and the near-a-river allowance
stopifnot(s_of("published")$grad_max == 0.13, s_of("minimal")$grad_max == 0.09,
          !in_reg("published", "minimal"), in_reg("minimal", "published"),
          s_of("parent")$pick == s_of("minimal")$pick, s_of("atlas")$grad_max > s_of("published")$grad_max,
          !in_reg("atlas", "published"), !in_reg("atlas", "minimal"),
          length(unique(sub("\\|g<=[0-9.]+\\|", "|", su$pick))) == 1)
d_on <- as.Date(substr(s_of("published")$tune_run, 1, 8), "%Y%m%d")
# the published setup is the full network reading each segment's own slope
stopifnot(s_of("published")$token_cut == "cut-full-top", s_of("published")$curve_grad == "segment_gradient")
hab_spread <- diff(range(su$tuned_km)) / max(su$tuned_km)
stopifnot(hab_spread < 0.03)
tuned_on <- paste(as.integer(format(d_on, "%d")), format(d_on, "%B %Y"))
# every close call changes all three parts of link's rule, on every setup
stopifnot(all(vapply(x$tune, function(t) all(t$departures[t$in_region == "TRUE"] == "3"), TRUE)))
# rules other than the chosen one with a given limit that are close calls on a setup's records
n_lim <- function(region_of, g) {
  t <- x$tune[[region_of]]
  sum(t$in_region == "TRUE" & as.numeric(t$grad_max) == g & t$rule != s_of("published")$pick)
}
stopifnot(n_lim("minimal", s_of("published")$grad_max) > 0)
tr <- x$transfer
transfer_pct <- tr$minimal_only_km / tr$minimal_km
# the net: the transferred rule's habitat against the minimal network's own
transfer_net <- 1 - tr$parent_km / tr$minimal_km
stopifnot(abs(tr$parent_km - s_of("parent")$tuned_km) < 0.05, transfer_pct < 0.02, tr$parent_only_km < tr$minimal_only_km,
          transfer_net > 0, transfer_net < transfer_pct)

# ---- the other keys ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ok <- x$other_keys
# chinook rearing is reported on its own above, so the sentence counts the others
stopifnot(nrow(ok) == 7, "CH_rear" %in% ok$key[ok$network_moved != "same"])
ok6 <- ok[ok$key != "CH_rear", ]
n_moved <- sum(ok6$network_moved != "same")
n_out <- sum(!ok6$minimal_in_full_region | !ok6$full_in_minimal_region)
stopifnot(nrow(ok6) == 6, n_moved == 3, n_out == 2)

# ---- the sites that change side ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
st <- x$sites
crit <- x$criteria
n_sites <- nrow(st)
n_fish <- sum(st$present)
# the two networks' own slopes (a full segment's minimal parent reads another slope at a few sites); the examples
# below are chosen on the parent's, as the bundle chose them
side <- function(g, t) g <= t
st$cross_m <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(crit$limits, function(t) side(st$full_gradient, t) != side(st$minimal_gradient, t)))
st$d <- st$full_gradient - st$minimal_gradient
cr <- st[st$cross_m, ]
steep <- function(g, present) mean(g[st$present == present] > crit$limits[["minimal"]])
# the tuning's sites: those in groups where chinook were caught at some sites and not others
both_out <- ave(st$present, st$watershed_group_code, FUN = function(p) any(p) && !all(p))
stopifnot(sum(both_out) == su$n_visits[1])
cr_scored <- st[st$cross_m & both_out, ]
n_groups <- length(unique(st$watershed_group_code[both_out]))
r_cross <- round(nrow(cr), -2)

stopifnot(sum(cr$present) < 10, sum(cr$d > 0) > 2 * sum(cr$d < 0),
          steep(st$full_gradient, FALSE) > steep(st$minimal_gradient, FALSE),
          steep(st$full_gradient, TRUE) > steep(st$minimal_gradient, TRUE))
```

The R package [`link`](`r link_site`) [@link] holds the recipes that turn what is known about each fish species' life
history into habitat on British Columbia's stream network. A recipe is a config, and every rule and threshold in it is
a row in a table. For each species and life stage it sets a **habitat definition**: the smallest stream the species
uses, the steepest slope it holds in, how close a large river must be for a smaller stream to likely be used as
habitat. It also defines what counts as an obstacle to fish passage, from falls and steep sections to the road and rail
crossings and dams below them. [`fresh`](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fresh) [@fresh], our stream network
modelling engine, runs the recipe: it cuts the streams of the BC Freshwater Atlas [@flnrord2021FreshwaterAtlasb] into
**segments**, works out which segments each species can reach, and classifies their habitat. So a model can be
changed, run beside another and traced back to the rules that produced it.

`knowledge`, the package this article belongs to, is our evidence tool for link's habitat definitions. It starts from
what is known about each species' life history, from the published literature and past reports, and the biology sets
the shape of a definition, such as young chinook rearing in small streams close to a large river. Where the Province's
fish sampling records are rich enough, they tune its values: knowledge scores candidate values against where sampling
caught the species and where it did not, keeps the smallest change to link's standard settings that fits about as well
as the best, and checks it on parts of the province it was not chosen from ([how the tuning
works](habitat_thresholds.html)). A habitat map steers where restoration and conservation effort goes, and one tuned
this way rests on where fish have actually been found.

Chinook rearing is the worked example here; [the research notes](`r research`) hold every species tuned, each run
behind this article and its checks.

A segment's slope is its drop over its whole length, so where a stream is cut decides the slope a habitat definition is
tested on, and some cuts fall exactly where fish were caught. Change the cuts and the definition chosen from those
catches can change. Chinook rearing's slope limit is **`r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)`** on link's full network and
**`r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)`** on its minimal network, which leaves out the cuts at fish records, at crossings
and at hand-mapped habitat. Yet the two definitions draw much the same habitat; on the map they differ in short pieces
of small streams:

```{r map-data}
mp <- x$map
mrow <- places[places$place == "map", ]
d <- mp$drawn
lv <- c("Both definitions", paste0("Full network's own slope (", lim(s_of("published")$grad_max), ") only"),
        paste0("Minimal network's slope (", lim(s_of("parent")$grad_max), ") only"))
d$cls <- factor(dplyr::case_when(d$published & d$parent ~ lv[1], d$published ~ lv[2], d$parent ~ lv[3]), levels = lv)
d <- d[!is.na(d$cls), ]
km_cls <- tapply(d$length_metre, d$cls, sum) / 1000
small <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), d$cls, function(i) sum(d$length_metre[i][d$stream_order[i] <= 3]) / sum(d$length_metre[i]))
# the words: much the same habitat, each rule's own km mostly on small streams (order 3 or less), the shared habitat
# under half
stopifnot(km_cls[[2]] > 2 * km_cls[[3]], km_cls[[1]] > 10 * (km_cls[[2]] + km_cls[[3]]),
          small[[2]] > 0.75, small[[3]] > 0.75, small[[1]] < 0.5)
d$lwd <- pmin(pmax(d$stream_order, 1), 6) / 3
# the zoom: of a 15 km grid from the group's south-west corner, the cell holding the most km drawn by one rule and not
# the other, each segment counted whole in the cell holding its centroid
cell <- 15000
bb <- sf::st_bbox(mp$background)
dif <- d[d$cls != lv[1], ]
mid <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_centroid(sf::st_geometry(dif)))
key <- paste(floor((mid[, "X"] - bb[["xmin"]]) / cell), floor((mid[, "Y"] - bb[["ymin"]]) / cell))
best <- names(which.max(tapply(dif$length_metre, key, sum)))
ij <- as.numeric(strsplit(best, " ")[[1]])
zoom <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = bb[["xmin"]] + ij[1] * cell, ymin = bb[["ymin"]] + ij[2] * cell,
                      xmax = bb[["xmin"]] + (ij[1] + 1) * cell, ymax = bb[["ymin"]] + (ij[2] + 1) * cell),
                    crs = sf::st_crs(mp$background))
km_zoom <- sum(dif$length_metre[key == best]) / 1000
# each panel is drawn on a canvas of its own box's shape, so tmap pads nothing and the scale bars hold: the group's
# extent as it is, and the cell widened about its centre to the zoom panel's shape
map_w <- 7
zoom_h <- 3.6
widen <- function(b, asp) {
  cx <- (b[["xmin"]] + b[["xmax"]]) / 2
  half_w <- max(b[["xmax"]] - b[["xmin"]], asp * (b[["ymax"]] - b[["ymin"]])) / 2
  half_h <- half_w / asp
  cy <- (b[["ymin"]] + b[["ymax"]]) / 2
  sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = cx - half_w, ymin = cy - half_h, xmax = cx + half_w, ymax = cy + half_h), crs = sf::st_crs(b))
}
zoom_box <- widen(zoom, map_w / zoom_h)
over_h <- map_w * (bb[["ymax"]] - bb[["ymin"]]) / (bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]])
stopifnot(zoom_box[["xmin"]] <= zoom[["xmin"]], zoom_box[["ymax"]] >= zoom[["ymax"]])
# the names: the group's largest streams on the upper panel, four chosen streams on the lower one
streams <- pl$streams
lab_over <- streams[streams$stream_order >= 6 & streams$km >= 20, ]
stopifnot("Fraser River" %in% lab_over$gnis_name, nrow(lab_over) >= 3)
```

```{r map, fig.height = round(over_h + zoom_h, 2), fig.cap = paste0("Chinook rearing habitat in the ", mrow$gnis_name, " watershed group, around the ", mrow$joins, " ", n0(mrow$town_km), " km ", mrow$compass, " of ", mrow$town, ", under two habitat definitions, both run on link's full network. Grey: drawn by both. Black: drawn only by the definition tuned on each segment's own slope (a ", lim(s_of("published")$grad_max), " limit). Steel blue: drawn only by the definition tuned on the minimal network, reading each segment's minimal-network slope (", lim(s_of("parent")$grad_max), "). Line width follows stream order. The lower panel enlarges the box outlined above. Stream names are the Freshwater Atlas's. Basemap: Esri World Topographic Map and World Shaded Relief.")}
# on the relief basemap the shared habitat is quiet and the two differences carry the map, each over a thin white casing
cols_map <- stats::setNames(unname(pal[c("mid", "ink", "accent")]), lv)
lab_col <- gq::gq_reg_main()$layers$stream_labels$label
# Esri's topographic map blended with its shaded relief, warped to BC Albers (as New Graph's habitat-rules post draws
# its maps); fetched when the article builds
basemap <- function(b, zoom_level) {
  g <- sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(sf::st_buffer(sf::st_as_sfc(b), 2000), 4326))
  topo <- gq::gq_basemap_tiles(g, provider = "Esri.WorldTopoMap", zoom = zoom_level, pad = 0, crs = 3005)
  relief <- gq::gq_basemap_tiles(g, provider = "Esri.WorldShadedRelief", zoom = zoom_level, pad = 0, crs = 3005)
  if (is.null(topo) || is.null(relief)) stop("the basemap tiles did not fetch")
  # faded toward white so the mark's black, greys and steel blue read over it
  gq::gq_basemap_blend(topo, relief, method = "gamma", gamma = 1) * 0.5 + 255 * 0.5
}
# one label per stream, on the straightest stretch of its longest run inside the panel, turned to its angle and set
# just off the channel (after the habitat-rules post)
stream_labels <- function(s, b, reach, off_m) {
  inner <- sf::st_as_sfc(b)
  x <- suppressWarnings(sf::st_intersection(s, sf::st_buffer(inner, -reach)))
  if (!nrow(x)) return(NULL)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(unique(x$gnis_name), function(n) {
    l <- sf::st_cast(sf::st_line_merge(sf::st_cast(sf::st_union(x[x$gnis_name == n, ]), "MULTILINESTRING")), "LINESTRING")
    l <- l[which.max(sf::st_length(l))]
    len <- as.numeric(sf::st_length(l))
    if (len < 2 * reach) return(NULL)
    pt <- function(p) sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_line_sample(l, sample = pmin(pmax(p, 0), 1)))[1, 1:2]
    dd <- reach / len
    at <- seq(0.2, 0.8, by = 0.05)
    straight <- vapply(at, function(p) sqrt(sum((pt(p + dd) - pt(p - dd))^2)) / (2 * dd * len), 0)
    p <- at[which.max(straight)]
    a <- pt(p - dd); z <- pt(p + dd)
    ang <- atan2(z[2] - a[2], z[1] - a[1]) * 180 / pi
    if (ang > 90) ang <- ang - 180
    if (ang <= -90) ang <- ang + 180
    off <- off_m * c(-sin(ang * pi / 180), cos(ang * pi / 180))
    sf::st_sf(name = n, ang = ang, geom = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_point(pt(p) + off), crs = sf::st_crs(s)))
  }))
}
# text with a thin white halo: tmap has none, so white copies sit behind the label
halo_text <- function(m, lab, size) {
  if (is.null(lab) || !nrow(lab)) return(m)
  m <- m + tmap::tm_shape(lab)
  for (o in list(c(1, 0), c(-1, 0), c(0, 1), c(0, -1), c(.7, .7), c(-.7, .7), c(.7, -.7), c(-.7, -.7))) {
    m <- m + tmap::tm_text("name", size = size, angle = "ang", fontface = "italic", col = "white",
                           xmod = o[1] * 0.04, ymod = o[2] * 0.04)
  }
  m + tmap::tm_text("name", size = size, angle = "ang", fontface = "italic", col = lab_col$color)
}
draw <- function(b, zoom_level, scale_km, lwd_add, labs, frame_box = NULL, legend = TRUE) {
  both <- d[d$cls == lv[1], ]
  dd <- d[d$cls != lv[1], ]
  dd$lwd <- dd$lwd + lwd_add
  m <- tmap::tm_shape(basemap(b, zoom_level), bbox = b) + tmap::tm_rgb() +
    tmap::tm_shape(both) + tmap::tm_lines(col = cols_map[[1]], lwd = "lwd",
                                          lwd.scale = tmap::tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 1),
                                          lwd.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide()) +
    tmap::tm_shape(dd) + tmap::tm_lines(col = "white", lwd = "lwd", lwd.scale = tmap::tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 2.6),
                                        lwd.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide()) +
    tmap::tm_shape(dd) +
    tmap::tm_lines(col = "cls", col.scale = tmap::tm_scale_categorical(values = cols_map, levels.drop = FALSE),
                   col.legend = if (legend) tmap::tm_legend(title = "Chinook rearing drawn by") else tmap::tm_legend_hide(),
                   lwd = "lwd", lwd.scale = tmap::tm_scale_continuous(values.scale = 1.6),
                   lwd.legend = tmap::tm_legend_hide())
  if (!is.null(frame_box)) m <- m + tmap::tm_shape(sf::st_as_sfc(frame_box)) + tmap::tm_borders(col = "black", lwd = 1.2)
  m <- halo_text(m, labs, 0.7)
  m + tmap::tm_scalebar(breaks = c(0, scale_km / 2, scale_km), position = tmap::tm_pos_in("right", "bottom"),
                        bg.color = "white", bg.alpha = 0.8) +
    tmap::tm_layout(frame = TRUE, inner.margins = 0, outer.margins = 0, legend.position = tmap::tm_pos_in("left", "bottom"),
                    legend.frame = TRUE, legend.bg.color = "white", legend.bg.alpha = 0.9)
}
w_over <- bb[["xmax"]] - bb[["xmin"]]
w_zoom <- zoom_box[["xmax"]] - zoom_box[["xmin"]]
lab_up <- stream_labels(lab_over, bb, reach = w_over / 60, off_m = w_over / 250)
# the lower panel names the main river and the three tributaries the differences sit on (Al's choice, 2026-11-05)
lab_names <- c("Fraser River", "Slim Creek", "Dome Creek", "Ptarmigan Creek")
in_zoom <- streams[streams$gnis_name %in% lab_names, ]
stopifnot(setequal(in_zoom$gnis_name[lengths(sf::st_intersects(in_zoom, sf::st_as_sfc(zoom_box))) > 0], lab_names))
lab_lo <- stream_labels(in_zoom, zoom_box, reach = w_zoom / 25, off_m = w_zoom / 250)
f_over <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
f_zoom <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
tmap::tmap_save(draw(bb, 9, 20, 1.2, lab_up, frame_box = zoom_box), f_over, width = map_w, height = over_h, dpi = 150)
tmap::tmap_save(draw(zoom_box, 12, 4, 2, lab_lo, legend = FALSE), f_zoom, width = map_w,
                height = zoom_h, dpi = 150)
grid::grid.newpage()
lay <- grid::grid.layout(2, 1, heights = grid::unit(c(over_h, zoom_h), "null"))
grid::pushViewport(grid::viewport(layout = lay))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f_over), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 1))
grid::grid.raster(png::readPNG(f_zoom), vp = grid::viewport(layout.pos.row = 2))
```

In the `r mrow$gnis_name` watershed group the two definitions draw `r n0(km_cls[[1]])` km of chinook rearing habitat alike.
The definition tuned on each segment's own slope adds `r n0(km_cls[[2]])` km, and the one tuned on the minimal network adds
`r n0(km_cls[[3]])` km. Most of each difference lies on small streams, of stream order 3 or less, against under half
of the habitat both draw. The group was chosen before drawing as the one where the tunings compared in this article
disagree over the most km.

## Why does a cut at a catch matter?

```{r profile-data}
cc <- x$concept
sg <- cc$segments
xmax <- 700
pr <- cc$atlas_profile[cc$atlas_profile$measure <= xmax + 50, ]
lab_net <- c(full = "Full network", minimal = "Minimal network", atlas = "Atlas line")
cols_net <- c("Full network" = unname(pal["ink"]), "Minimal network" = unname(pal["accent"]), "Atlas line" = unname(pal["grey"]))
sg$net <- factor(lab_net[sg$network], levels = lab_net)
site_seg <- sg[sg$from_m <= cc$site$measure & sg$to_m > cc$site$measure, ]
stopifnot(nrow(site_seg) == 3, setequal(site_seg$network, names(lab_net)))
seg_at <- function(n) site_seg[site_seg$network == n, ]
# the profile's words: the full network cuts at the catch, so the site starts a segment of its own, steeper than its
# minimal segment and gentler than the whole Atlas line
stopifnot(abs(seg_at("full")$from_m - cc$site$measure) < 1, cc$site$present,
          abs(seg_at("full")$gradient - cc$site$full_gradient) < 1e-4,
          abs(seg_at("minimal")$gradient - cc$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4,
          seg_at("full")$gradient > crit$limits[["minimal"]], seg_at("minimal")$gradient < crit$limits[["minimal"]],
          seg_at("atlas")$gradient > crit$limits[["published"]], seg_at("minimal")$from_m < 50,
          seg_at("atlas")$z_up > 1040)  # the caption: the Atlas line runs past the top of the figure
cc_sites <- cc$sites
cc_sites$z <- stats::approx(pr$measure, pr$z, cc_sites$measure)$y
site_seg$lab <- sprintf("%s: %s over %s", site_seg$net, grad(site_seg$gradient),
                        ifelse(site_seg$length_metre >= 1000, paste(formatC(site_seg$length_metre / 1000, format = "f", digits = 1), "km"),
                               paste(n0(site_seg$length_metre), "m")))
```

Both of link's networks cut a stream where one Atlas line meets the next, at natural barriers and at the steep sections
a species cannot pass. The full network adds cuts the minimal network does not make, among them crossings, the ends of
stretches whose habitat has been mapped by hand, and records of the species link models in each watershed group (in the
build used here, each such species' highest record on each stream, drawn from bcfishobs
[@norris2024smnorrisbcfishobs]). link cuts at those records so that a segment can say whether the species has been
seen at or above it, as bcfishpass [@norris2024smnorrisbcfishpass] does. Every habitat definition is then tested on the
slope of the shorter segment.

An electrofishing visit that caught fish is often such a record, so the cut lands at the visit, and the slope tested
there is worked out from the visit upstream. On the stream below, the visit that caught chinook reads
`r grad(seg_at("full")$gradient)` on the full network, over the `r n0(seg_at("full")$length_metre)` m above it, and
`r grad(seg_at("minimal")$gradient)` on the minimal network, whose segment runs from near the mouth past the visit.

```{r profile, fig.height = 3.6, fig.cap = paste0("One stream cut two ways: ", where(list(place = "concept", site_visit = cc$site$site_visit)), ". The thin grey line is the stream's elevation along its Atlas line. Each coloured line is a segment drawn as the straight slope tested on it, with ticks at the ends of the full and minimal networks' segments: black the full network's, steel blue the minimal network's, grey the whole Atlas line's, which runs on past the top of the figure. The black dot is a visit where chinook were caught; the open circle, on the same full-network segment, a visit where none were. The labels give the slope each version reads at the black dot. Elevation is stretched several times so the slopes can be seen.")}
lab_pos <- data.frame(net = site_seg$net, lab = site_seg$lab,
                      x = c(full = 440, minimal = 330, atlas = 300)[site_seg$network],
                      y = c(full = 994.5, minimal = 1016, atlas = 1036)[site_seg$network])
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = pr, aes(measure, z), colour = "grey78", linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_segment(data = sg, aes(x = from_m, xend = to_m, y = z_dn, yend = z_up, colour = net), linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_point(data = sg[sg$network != "atlas", ], aes(x = from_m, y = z_dn, colour = net), shape = 124, size = 2.2,
             show.legend = FALSE) +

             show.legend = FALSE) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = cols_net, name = NULL) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.height = grid::unit(0.6, "lines"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey92", linewidth = 0.25),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3), axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "grey25"), axis.text = element_text(colour = "grey35"))
```

```{r strip-data}
cls_lab <- c(paste(lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]]), "or less"),
             paste("over", lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]]), "to", lim(crit$limits[["published"]])),
             paste("over", lim(crit$limits[["published"]])))
cols_cls <- stats::setNames(unname(pal[c("light", "mid", "ink")]), cls_lab)
half <- 600
ex <- x$examples
stopifnot(length(ex) == crit$n_examples)
# each example meets the criteria the bundle chose it by: chinook caught, a full segment of at least min_len_m, its
# slope and its minimal parent's on opposite sides of a tuned limit, one per group
for (e in ex) {
  stopifnot(e$site$present, e$site$crosses, e$site$full_length_m >= crit$min_len_m,
            e$site$watershed_group_code != cc$site$watershed_group_code,
            abs(e$site$parent_gradient - e$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4,
            e$site$full_length_m < e$site$minimal_length_m)
}
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(ex, function(e) e$site$watershed_group_code, ""))) == length(ex))
ex_lab <- vapply(ex, function(e) {
  w <- where(list(place = "example", site_visit = e$site$site_visit))
  paste0(toupper(substr(w, 1, 1)), substr(w, 2, nchar(w)))
}, "")
strip <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(ex), function(i) {
  e <- ex[[i]]
  s <- sf::st_drop_geometry(e$segments)
  s |> transmute(ex = ex_lab[[i]],
                 net = c(full = "Full network", minimal = "Minimal network")[network],
                 from = downstream_route_measure - e$site$measure, to = from + length_metre, gradient)
}))
strip <- strip |>
  filter(to > -half, from < half) |>
  mutate(at_site = from <= 0 & to > 0,
         from = pmax(from, -half), to = pmin(to, half),
         cls = factor(cut(gradient, c(-Inf, crit$limits[["minimal"]], crit$limits[["published"]], Inf), labels = cls_lab),
                      levels = cls_lab),
         y = ifelse(net == "Full network", 2, 1),
         ex = factor(ex, levels = unname(ex_lab)))
# the caption: a bar that stops short of the left edge stops at the stream's mouth
for (e in ex) {
  if (e$site$measure < half) stopifnot(min(e$segments$downstream_route_measure) < 1)
}
# the slope each network reads at the site is the one the site's record holds
for (i in seq_along(ex)) {
  s <- strip[strip$ex %in% ex_lab[[i]] & strip$at_site, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == 2,
            abs(s$gradient[s$net == "Full network"] - ex[[i]]$site$full_gradient) < 1e-4,
            abs(s$gradient[s$net == "Minimal network"] - ex[[i]]$site$minimal_gradient) < 1e-4)
}
```

The same happens elsewhere. Three more visits with chinook show how far the cut can move the slope tested. In
each of three watershed groups, they are the visit where the two networks' slopes differ most while sitting on
opposite sides of a tuned limit, picked by criteria set before drawing:

```{r strip, fig.height = 3.4, fig.cap = paste0("The segments around three visits where chinook were caught, as each network cuts them, from ", half, " m below the visit to ", half, " m above it (a bar that stops short of the left edge stops at the stream's mouth). Each bar is a segment, coloured by the slope tested on it; the line marks the visit, and the slope each network reads there is labelled beside it. The panel titles name each stream, the river it flows or drains into and the nearest town. The criteria: among visits with chinook whose full-network slope and the slope of the minimal-network segment it lies within sit on opposite sides of a tuned limit, on a full-network segment at least ", crit$min_len_m, " m long and outside the watershed group of the stream in the figure above, the largest gap in each group, from the ", crit$n_examples, " groups with the largest gaps.")}
at_site <- strip[strip$at_site, ]
# each printed slope (two decimals) falls on the same side of each limit as its bar's colour
stopifnot(all(vapply(crit$limits, function(t) all((round(at_site$gradient, 4) <= t) == (at_site$gradient <= t)), TRUE)))
ggplot(strip) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = from, xmax = to, ymin = y - 0.22, ymax = y + 0.22, fill = cls), colour = "white",
            linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.4, colour = "grey25") +
  geom_label(data = at_site, aes(x = 16, y = y, label = grad(gradient, 2)), hjust = 0, size = 2.7, colour = "grey15",
             fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = grid::unit(0.12, "lines"), alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = 1:2, labels = c("Minimal network", "Full network"), limits = c(0.7, 2.3)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols_cls, drop = FALSE, name = "Slope tested") +
  facet_wrap(~ex, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Distance upstream of the visit (m)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "grey30"), panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.6, "lines"))
```

```{r strip-words}
# the paragraph below: two of the three read steeper on the full network; on the third the full segment ends above the
# site, below steeper water that the minimal segment averages in
steeper <- vapply(ex, function(e) e$site$full_gradient > e$site$minimal_gradient, TRUE)
stopifnot(sum(steeper) == 2)
g3 <- ex[[which(!steeper)]]
ord3 <- c("first", "second", "third")[which(!steeper)]
s3 <- sf::st_drop_geometry(g3$segments)
top3 <- g3$site$full_offset_m + g3$site$full_length_m
above3 <- s3[s3$network == "full" & abs(s3$downstream_route_measure - (g3$site$measure + top3)) < 1, ]
stopifnot(nrow(above3) == 1, above3$gradient > g3$site$minimal_gradient,
          g3$site$minimal_offset_m + g3$site$minimal_length_m > top3 + above3$length_metre / 2)
```

The shorter segment does not always read the steeper slope. In the `r ord3` panel, the full network's segment ends
`r n0(top3)` m above the visit, and the steeper water above it, which the minimal network's segment averages in, is
read on its own.

How often does it happen? If link cut visits with fish and visits without alike, a slope limit would be judged on the
same footing at both. On the full network it does not: a visit that caught fish starts a segment of its own far more
often than one that caught none. The minimal network takes that difference away.

```{r premise, fig.height = 2.6, fig.cap = paste0("Electrofishing visits that start a segment of their own, on three of link's networks: dark, visits where fish of any species were caught; light, visits where none were. A visit starts its own segment when the segment begins between 1 m below it and 5 m above it. The same ", n0(sum(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal"])), " visits are counted on each network (", n0(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal" & pm$catch_status == "fish"]), " with fish, ", n0(pm$visits[pm$network == "minimal" & pm$catch_status == "zero"]), " without): those with a fished area in the usual range, on the stream lines the tuning scores. The networks are link ", unique(pm$link[pm$network == "published_92"]), "'s, link ", unique(pm$link[pm$network == "published_145"]), "'s and link ", unique(pm$link[pm$network == "minimal"]), "'s.")}
lab_pm <- c(published_92 = "An earlier full network,\ncut at every record",
            published_145 = "The full network used here, cut at each\nspecies' highest record on a stream",
            minimal = "The minimal network, no cuts at\nrecords, crossings or mapped habitat")
cols_catch <- c("Visits with fish" = unname(pal["ink"]), "Visits without" = unname(pal["soft"]))
bars <- data.frame(net = factor(unname(lab_pm[pm$network]), levels = rev(unname(lab_pm))),
                   who = factor(ifelse(pm$catch_status == "fish", "Visits with fish", "Visits without"),
                                levels = names(cols_catch)),
                   share = pm$at_site_pct / 100)
ggplot(bars, aes(share, net, fill = who)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge2(width = 0.75, reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pc(share, 1)), position = position_dodge2(width = 0.75, reverse = TRUE), hjust = -0.15,
            size = 2.7, colour = "grey25") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cols_catch, name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0), labels = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9.5) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.size = grid::unit(0.6, "lines"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "grey25", lineheight = 0.9))
```

Visits without chinook move too. Of the roughly `r n0(round(n_sites, -2))` visits in chinook's range that the tuning
starts from, the two networks put the slope on opposite sides of `r lim(crit$limits[["minimal"]])` or
`r lim(crit$limits[["published"]])` at about `r n0(r_cross)`, and only `r sum(cr$present)` of those caught chinook. These runs do not say which of the full network's
cuts move them.

## How does the tuning choose a habitat definition?

A habitat definition decides how much habitat link draws, so it should be one the fish records support. The tuning
tries many candidate definitions, each a different set of parameters, and scores each by how well it predicts where chinook were caught in watershed groups left out of the
fit; lower is better. For chinook rearing it scored about `r n0(round(su$n_visits[1], -2))` visits in
`r n_groups` watershed groups. A score carries error, so every candidate within one standard error of the best is a
**close call**: the records cannot rank close calls apart. For chinook rearing the tuning varies the three parts of the definition:
the smallest stream (by flow or by channel width), the steepest slope, and the allowance near a large river (how large
the river, and how close). Of the close calls the
tuning chooses the one closest to link's standard settings for the species, and among equals the best scorer; for
chinook rearing every close call differs from link's standard settings in all three parts, so the choice is the best
scorer.

## What does each network choose?

Chinook rearing was tuned four ways, on the same visits, flows and species range, so that the segments and the slope tested are
the only differences. Two of the four read a slope from somewhere else onto the full network's segments:
each segment's **minimal parent**, the minimal-network segment it lies within, and the whole Atlas line it lies on.

```{r setups}
how <- c(published = "link's full network, each segment reading its own slope (how link applies a habitat definition)",
         minimal = "link's minimal network, without the cuts at fish records, crossings and hand-mapped habitat",
         parent = "The full network's segments, each reading its minimal parent's slope",
         atlas = "The full network's segments, each reading the slope of the whole Atlas line it lies on")
yn <- function(v) ifelse(v, "yes", "no")
tb <- data.frame(`Segments and slope` = unname(how[su$setup]),
                 `Slope limit chosen` = lim(su$grad_max),
                 `A close call on the full network's records?` = yn(vapply(su$setup, in_reg, TRUE, region_of = "published")),
                 `On the minimal network's?` = yn(vapply(su$setup, in_reg, TRUE, region_of = "minimal")),
                 check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tb, format = "html", align = "lrcc", row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "The chinook rearing habitat definition chosen on each network and slope.") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, font_size = 13) |>
  kableExtra::footnote(general_title = "", general = paste0(
    "Every definition chosen keeps the same flow floor and the same allowance for small streams near a large river; only the ",
    "slope limit differs. A verdict is on the definition chosen, not on its limit alone: on the minimal network's records, ",
    n_lim("minimal", s_of("published")$grad_max), " other candidates with a ", lim(s_of("published")$grad_max),
    " limit, differing in their flow floor or their allowance, are close calls."))
```

Without the full network's extra cuts, the records argue for the gentler limit. Read on the full network's own slopes,
they choose
`r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)`, and that definition is not a close call on the minimal network's records. Without those
cuts they choose `r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)`, which is a close call on the full network's records as well. Given
each segment's minimal parent's slope, the full network chooses the minimal network's definition exactly. The Atlas line's
slopes choose `r lim(s_of("atlas")$grad_max)`, in a definition that is a close call on neither network's records; these
runs do not show why. The habitat each definition draws, run through all of link's steps on the segments it was tuned on,
differs by under `r pc(ceiling(100 * hab_spread) / 100)` across the four.

## What does it mean for someone using the thresholds?

This package's chinook rearing thresholds, tuned on `r tuned_on`, were tuned on link's full network, each segment
reading its own slope, which is how link applies a habitat definition. On another network, or with slopes read another way, the same
chinook records choose another definition: the slope limit reads `r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)`,
`r lim(s_of("minimal")$grad_max)` or `r lim(s_of("atlas")$grad_max)`, while the flow floor and the allowance near large
rivers hold on all four. The records do not make one limit right everywhere: each is the best fit for the slopes it was
tuned on, and the published `r lim(s_of("published")$grad_max)` was tuned on the slopes link applies it to.

A definition tuned on the minimal network can still be run on the full one, by giving each full segment its minimal parent's
slope. For chinook rearing it then draws `r pc(transfer_net, 1)` less habitat than on the minimal network itself. The
stretches only the minimal network draws are small streams near large rivers, because the allowance measures its
distance from a segment's downstream end.

## Limits

- These runs tuned chinook rearing all four ways, and the `r nrow(ok6)` other species and stages both networks could
  fit on the two networks' own slopes and, in a separate check, on the Atlas line each visit lies on
  ([the methodology article's limits](habitat_thresholds.html#limits)). The network moved the definition for some of those
  too.
- The minimal network leaves out the cuts at fish records, at crossings and at hand-mapped habitat together, so these
  runs cannot say which of the three moved the limit. Builds that each leave out one kind of cut would.
- Few visits carry the difference: of the roughly `r n0(round(su$n_visits[1], -2))` visits the tunings scored,
  `r n0(nrow(cr_scored))` read a slope on opposite
  sides of a chosen limit on the two networks, and `r sum(cr_scored$present)` of those caught chinook. The runs show
  that the network moves the choice, not which visits move it.
- Slopes taken over a fixed length of stream, which would not depend on where fish were caught, were not tested.

## How was this done?

The numbers were bundled on `r x$meta$written` from the tuning runs and link builds the research notes
describe. When it was written, the share of visits starting their own segment, the four tunings'
choices and habitat, and the other species' choices were checked against the logs that report them there. The visits are the
Fisheries Data Information System's electrofishing records [@provinceofbritishcolumbia2022FisheriesData], placed on
the Freshwater Atlas; fresh runs link's habitat definitions. The maps' basemap is Esri's World Topographic Map
blended with its World Shaded Relief.
